title: Psalms (Part 3)
hook: There's a moment buried in Psalm 110 that early Christians couldn't stop quoting: David—Israel's greatest king, the one every future monarch would be measured against—looks up and calls someone else "my lord." Not a rival king. Not an angel. Someone who outranks him entirely. It's a strange, almost impossible line for a king to write about himself, and it's exactly why this collection of psalms rewards slow, careful attention rather than a quick skim. Sandwiched between that royal paradox are some of the rawest lines in scripture—a nameless sufferer commanding his own faint soul to praise God, an afflicted heart pouring out its complaint at the temple gates, a psalmist who has to talk himself back into peace after nearly drowning in despair. What emerges isn't tidy theology; it's the sound of real people wrestling their way toward hope, and finding, again and again, that God was already there waiting. Sit with these words long enough and you may find your own soul being commanded to do the same.
